_comment: Canonical §37 Listener settings, read by BOTH sides:
- tests/unit/control/listener-settings-ipc-contract.test.ts drives the real
adapter in src/control/services/settings-listener.ts;
- src-tauri/tests/ipc_contract_tests.rs drives the real Rust struct in
src-tauri/src/settings/mod.rs.
This feature previously had TWO settings structures. Rust declared
opacityAfterDim / saturation / blurPx / scale / crossfadeMs / softPause /
hardPause / hideOnBlank; the TypeScript side typed the whole section as
Record<string, unknown> and mapped none of it, keeping its own
defaultPackId / autoplay / dimPercent in a localStorage overlay that nothing
read. Neither structure could be observed from the other side, which is
exactly what a fixture shared by both halves makes impossible.
Every value is deliberately NON-DEFAULT (defaults: null / true / 40 / 0 /
0.85). A field one side maps and the other does not comes back as its
default and the assertion fails naming it.
`settings` is simultaneously the UI view, the patch the UI emits for a
full-section write, and the document Rust stores — one shape on purpose.
Forgetting the remembered pack. `null` must be SENT, not omitted: Rust's
merge_json removes a key whose patch value is null and the container's
serde(default) refills it with None. Dropping the key would leave the old
pack id in the document, and the next session would open a Listener the
user had just turned off.
The ranges Rust validates, which are the ranges the Preflight sliders
offer. They used to disagree in both directions: opacityAfterDim <= 0.75
rejected a dim of 0, and blurPx <= 12 rejected the top half of a slider
that goes to 24 — so a value the UI could produce was a value Rust would
refuse to store. The adapter clamps rather than throwing.
